title: C12 · The scary number that had already stopped mattering
anchor: A figure carried for five weeks before being checked at the source, September 2026

slides.headline: THE SCARY NUMBER THAT HAD ALREADY STOPPED MATTERING
slides.sub: I carried it around for five weeks like a debt. Then I looked, and it had already been paid.
slides.boundary: No figures from anybody else's business appear in this document.

slides.label: weeks of low grade dread, against the ninety seconds it took to check once I finally did.
slides.sub: Nobody was hiding it from me. I had simply decided in advance what the answer was going to be.
slides.boundary: The number itself turned out to be old.

items.text: You hear it once, in a hurry, from a system you trust
You build a plan around it instead of checking it
Checking now means admitting you planned on a guess
The dread becomes the reason not to look
The number changes and nothing tells you

slides.boundary: Step three is where it actually gets expensive.

left.p: Handled, resolved, closed. It had stopped being true weeks before I got around to being afraid of it.

right.p: Decisions deferred, a plan built sideways around a thing that was not there, and attention spent on nothing.

slides.boundary: The carrying cost exceeded the number. That is the part worth saying out loud.

slides.quote: Go and look. A number you are afraid of is a number you have stopped measuring, and it is probably no longer the number.
slides.src: The same instinct that made me count fill rates instead of trusting a report.
slides.boundary: Every claim in my posts carries a date for exactly this reason.

lede: Anything I am avoiding gets a date and a source written next to it. If I cannot say where a number came from and when, it is not a number, it is a mood.
And the check goes in the calendar the same afternoon, because the whole failure mode is the deferral rather than the arithmetic.
slides.boundary: Dated at the source, or it does not get quoted.

items.text: The receivable you are sure is still outstanding
The client you assume has left
The subscription you think you need

slides.boundary: One afternoon, three checks, and at least one of them will be out of date.

slides.h2: THE SYSTEM THAT MAKES ME LOOK
lede: Every stale deal gets four questions every fourteen days, and every answer writes a record. Promo shops can request access.
